evals.prompt: Review my CloudFront distribution E1EXAMPLEDIST0 for best practices.
evals.expected_output: A prioritized operational review of the distribution that identifies the most urgent issue and explains why, cites specific configuration and CloudWatch-metric findings for this distribution, spans multiple Well-Architected concerns (security, reliability, performance, cost, operational excellence), and gives ordered read-only remediation recommendations.
assertions: The response identifies the single most urgent or highest-severity issue with the distribution and explains why it matters, rather than presenting every observation with equal weight
The response orders or groups its recommendations by urgency (for example, immediate actions versus later improvements) instead of giving one flat, undifferentiated list

The response covers more than one operational dimension — at least security and reliability, plus at least one of performance, cost, or operational excellence — rather than focusing on a single aspect

The recommendations are specific to this distribution's real configuration or metrics — naming the actual misconfigured setting, origin, viewer-protocol/TLS value, or error-rate figure — rather than generic CloudFront best-practice tips that would apply to any distribution
The response confines itself to read-only analysis and recommendations and does not perform, or claim to have performed, any change to the distribution

evals.prompt: Audit the security of my CloudFront distribution E1EXAMPLEDIST0 — WAF, TLS, and origin access.
evals.expected_output: A security-focused assessment of the distribution that checks WAF web ACL association, the viewer TLS minimum protocol version and viewer protocol policy, and how origins are protected (Origin Access Control versus a publicly reachable S3 origin), flags each gap with a severity, and gives concrete read-only remediation steps.
assertions: The response checks whether a WAF web ACL is associated with the distribution and calls out its absence as a risk when none is attached
The response evaluates the viewer-facing TLS posture — the minimum protocol version and whether plain HTTP is redirected or disallowed via the viewer protocol policy
The response examines how the origins are secured — for an S3 origin, whether Origin Access Control (or legacy OAI) is used rather than the bucket being publicly reachable
Each security gap it reports carries a severity or priority and a concrete, read-only remediation step rather than a vague suggestion
The response stays within read-only analysis and does not perform, or claim to have performed, any change to the distribution
